newsitem.title: FRANCE: Ugandan president to discuss Zaire in Paris visit.
newsitem.headline: Ugandan president to discuss Zaire in Paris visit.

text.p: Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni, a key player in the Zaire crisis, is expected in Paris on Tuesday for talks on the explosive situation in the Great Lakes area of central Africa, French officials said on Friday.
Museveni has also been invited for talks at the European Commission in Brussels, as has Kenyan President Daniel Arap Moi.

The two do not see eye-to-eye on the situation in the Great Lakes region where Zairean rebels battling government forces have seized extensive territory and in the process exacerbated the plight of tens of thousands of Rwandan Hutu refugees.
Uganda has been accused by Zaire of sending troops into Zaire to back the mostly Tutsi rebels advancing on four fronts against government forces.
French officials are also to confer with Burundi Foreign Minister Luc Rukingama whose country is also enmeshed in the crisis.
France, which has traditionally backed Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko, said on Thursday it was "paying special attention" to the presence of foreign troops in Zaire.
The United States on Wednesday said it had urged Uganda, Rwanda and Burundi to stay out of the fighting in east Zaire.
Kinshasa has accused all three of sending their troops into eastern Zaire to fight alongside the rebels. All three countries, which border on rebel-held territory, deny doing so.
Paris said it agreed with Washington that the participation of foreign forces in the Zaire conflict would create "an extremely serious situation."
A Foreign Ministry statement reiterated France's backing for an international conference on the crisis and for a referendum and elections in Zaire
